Hi Soojin / Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo today — good overview. A couple of things came up from our compliance team that I want to flag before we get too far down procurement:

- NordicHealth must ensure PHI and related metadata for EU patients never leave the EU for processing or storage (including logs).
- We have clinics in Singapore and Malaysia that would benefit from an APAC endpoint for latency, but data for EU patients must remain in EU.
- Does your hosted API guarantee EU-only residency (requests, logs, backups) if we select an EU region? Or do you still replicate telemetry to a US region?
- If hosted cannot guarantee EU-only, we need a Private/VPC or on-prem option — how different are lead times and pricing?

Pilot timeline: we are aiming for a 6‑8 week pilot for triage/chat workflows; compliance sign-off is the gating item.

Can you confirm the above and outline next steps? I can loop in Karin from compliance if helpful.

Cheers,
Lars
Director of Digital Services
NordicHealth AB

Lars / Maria — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so everyone is aligned (inc internal SE):

Summary of requirements (as we understood them)
- EU data residency for production (PHI and metadata cannot leave EU).
- APAC endpoints for Singapore/Malaysia clinics for latency-sensitive user flows — but EU patient data must remain in EU.
- Encryption at rest + KMS integration; audit logs for retention 24 months (compliance requirement).
- Pilot: 6–8 weeks, scope = triage + clinician-assist chat.

Redwood options and short notes
- Hosted API (fastest to launch): we offer region pinning for hosted customers. If you choose EU-hosted mode we can pin compute, storage, and logs to EU regions. We will provide DPA + data flow diagrams.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): deployable in a cloud region you select (EU) with customer isolation for predictable throughput and contractual SLAs. Works well if you need higher throughput and predictable cost.
- Private (VPC / on‑prem): supports customer-managed networking and KMS; on‑prem is possible for strict regulatory needs but will increase lead time and engagement scope.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm whether the primary pilot will process EU patient data only, or if anonymized/synthetic data will be used?
2) We recommend a short technical deep‑dive with Aditya (SE) to review network requirements, KMS, and data flow — can you share 2x 60‑minute slots next week?
3) I attached our latest region matrix and an initial SOW template to give rough lead times and cost bands.
4) We'll assemble a redacted SOC2 snapshot and a sample DPA for your legal/compliance review.

Attachments: redwood-region-matrix-2026-02.pdf, initial-sow-template.docx
Related links: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/9841, https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-pilot

Proposed tentative timeline
- Week 1: technical deep‑dive + compliance packet delivered
- Week 2–3: environment prep (EU-hosted pinning or dedicated cluster provisioning)
- Week 4–8: pilot execution

If EU-hosted pinning satisfies Karin's compliance requirements, Hosted is the fastest path; if not, Dedicated or Private are available but with longer lead times.

Thanks — looping in Aditya to pick times for the SE call.

Best,

Subject: RE: EU/APAC residency and deployment options — technical follow-up

Hi Lars / Maria — Aditya from SE team here. Quick technical clarifications to help your compliance review:

1) EU-hosted mode details
- We can guarantee compute, persistent storage, and standard audit logs are pinned to EU regions (currently eu-west-1 and eu-central-1).
- Backups and snapshots for EU-hosted mode remain in the EU; we do not replicate customer request payloads to US regions for analytics or debugging unless explicit cross-region backup is requested in contract.
- Telemetry for platform health may be aggregated (non‑PII) across regions for outage detection; we can scope what telemetry leaves region in the DPA.

2) Cross-region and APAC latency
- For APAC clinics we recommend a mixed strategy: EU-hosted for EU patient data + a regional APAC dedicated instance for low-latency chat for APAC patients. Requests for EU patients routed to EU hosts; APAC patients routed to APAC hosts.
- If you need a single global endpoint, we can implement routing policies but that will require clear operational SLOs and may complicate residency guarantees.

3) Dedicated vs Private vs On‑prem lead times (high level)
- Hosted (EU pinning): 1–2 weeks to enable DPA and region pinning for a pilot (fastest).
- Dedicated (reserved cluster in EU): 3–5 weeks (provisioning GPUs, network peering, capacity enrollment).
- Private VPC: 4–6 weeks for VPC connectivity, KMS integration, and compliance checks.
- On‑prem: 8–12+ weeks depending on hardware and local IT coordination.

4) Security controls
- We support customer KMS keys (AWS KMS / customer BYOK) for dedicated/private modes; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS or bring keys via partner HSMs for private deployments on request.
- Audit logs, retention policies, and forwarding to a customer SIEM via syslog are supported for Dedicated/Private.

I attached a short network checklist to speed the SE call. For the deep‑dive, available slots (CET): 2026-02-08 09:00, 2026-02-08 14:00, 2026-02-09 11:00. Which works for your team?

Attachment: network-checklist.csv

Thanks — happy to go through concrete data flow diagrams on the call.
